impact:
README advertises Windows x64/arm64 as supported (README.md:58), but `expandUser` (src/context.ts) implements CPython's POSIX `posixpath.expanduser` on every platform. On Windows, usage.py would instead go through `ntpath.expanduser`, which differs in four measurable ways:

1. It does NOT consult `HOME` at all — it reads `USERPROFILE`, falling back to `HOMEDRIVE` + `HOMEPATH`, and returns the path UNEXPANDED if neither is set.
2. It treats both `/` and `\` as separators when locating the end of the `~` component.
3. `~user` is resolved by replacing the basename of the resolved home, not via a passwd lookup — so it can succeed on Windows where the port refuses (ALLOWLIST entry 10).
4. The POSIX `userhome.rstrip('/')` and trailing `or '/'` rules do not apply.

Consequence: on Windows the port can resolve a DIFFERENT `CODEX_HOME` than usage.py and therefore read a different session tree, and `homeEnc` can encode a different home so project attribution differs. This is a real behavioural divergence on an advertised platform, not merely an unmeasured one.

Found by code review R7 (codex) during T-006. Filed rather than fixed: `expandUser` predates T-006 (it came from T-003) and T-006 only corrected the POSIX rstrip / empty-HOME tails, so ntpath support is out of this ticket's scope. It also cannot be verified here — the reference CPython is never run on Windows in this project, so any implementation would be unmeasured until a Windows parity run exists.

Resolution options, in preference order:
(a) Implement platform-aware expansion mirroring `ntpath.expanduser`, with table-driven tests that inject `platform` + an environment map so every branch is testable from one host — the same shape as PLATFORM_PACKAGES in resolve-ccusage.ts.
(b) If Windows parity is not going to be supported, qualify the README support table so it does not claim more than is true.

Recorded as a KNOWN GAP in ALLOWLIST entry 17 (it is deliberately not written as a sanctioned delta, because sanctioning a divergence on an advertised platform would be overclaiming).
title: Windows `~` expansion uses POSIX semantics, diverging from Python's ntpath.expanduser
